ProjectQr__Description: Project QR Code: one QR symbol per project, carrying a short address that opens the project's live ValeVision model, printed automatically on every document in the pack so anybody holding a drawing can scan straight into 3D. The symbol is the same on every sheet of a project and different for every project. SWITCHED OFF IN VALEVISION until Adam picks a Vale resolver (DR-12): Enabled is false and BaseUrl and IndexUrl are empty, so no document draws a code. Every value here is a built-in default mirrored in Na__ProjectQr__Symbol__.js, and a file that cannot be read switches the system off: a failed fetch draws no code rather than a code nobody chose. WHERE a document puts the code is that document's business: the drawing title block's cell is sized in Na__LayoutEditor__AppConfig__.json under LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config (QrCell...), whose LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__QrCellEnabled is false as well.
ProjectQr__PortedFrom: TrueVision3D 02__Src__AppModules/51__System__LayoutEditor/53__Feature__ProjectQrCode/Na__ProjectQr__Config__.json as TrueVision3D v2.120.0 shipped it (21-Sep-2026; read at HEAD b2aa9151), ported 02-Oct-2026 (parity package W1-15). Every other key is TrueVision's. ValeVision's values: Enabled false, BaseUrl and IndexUrl empty (DR-12 (A): no Vale resolver yet), and the notes on the address, the key and the index. The symbol's colours, quiet zone and print floor and the note's words are TrueVision's (DR-43: the note names no app).
ProjectQr__EnabledNote: False draws no code anywhere: every document asks this system for the symbol and draws nothing when it is given none. The title block then gives the cell's room back to the fields. VALEVISION SHIPS IT FALSE (DR-12 (A)) until a Vale resolver exists. Switching it on is package W5-05, together with Link BaseUrl and IndexUrl, a permanent qrKey on every master-index entry, and LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__QrCellEnabled in the title block's config.

ProjectQr__Link__Config.ProjectQr__Link__Description: The address a scanned code opens. A PRINTED CODE OUTLIVES EVERYTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY - it sits in a site bag or a planning file for years - so whatever form is printed has to go on being answered for good.
ProjectQr__Link__Config.ProjectQr__Link__BaseUrlNote: EMPTY: VALEVISION HAS NO RESOLVER YET (DR-12). An empty base builds no address, so no code is drawn even with Enabled true - and Na__ProjectQr__Symbol__.js reads an empty value here as absent and falls back to its own built-in base, which is empty too. When Adam picks the resolver (package W5-05; the candidate is a q/ page on ValeCodebase's GitHub Pages, beside the Lantern Designer's t/ terms resolver) this is its address. THE RESOLVER, NOT THE APP, AND ALWAYS THE LIVE SITE: a flat page that looks the project's key up in its index and sends the phone on to the project's full ValeVision address. It is never window.location: drawings are authored and exported on localhost (the editor is read-only on the web), and a code reading http://localhost:8000/... opens on the authoring machine and on no phone in the world. Once a code is printed, the resolver's folder must never be moved, renamed or removed.
ProjectQr__Link__Config.ProjectQr__Link__QueryPatternNote: Tokens: projectCode, projectFolder, year, each URL-encoded. In ValeVision projectCode is the project's RESOLVER KEY: the permanent qrKey of its master-index entry, written once by the index writer and kept through a rename (DR-12; package W5-05 writes them) - never the ?project= token on the address bar, which is usually a whole folderId and changes on a rename, and never the bare project code, which thirteen Vale projects share with a sibling scheme. projectFolder and year are the folder and four-digit year of the same master-index entry (Na__ProjectQr__ProjectLink__.js). A token the pattern asks for that the project cannot supply draws NO code, because a code that scans to a broken address is worse than none - so until the keys exist, no project has a code. The bare key is the whole query: no key name, no equals sign. If this pattern is ever changed once codes are printed, the resolver must go on answering the old form, because it is already on paper.
ProjectQr__Link__Config.ProjectQr__Link__LengthNote: WHY THE ADDRESS HAS TO BE SHORT. Encoded length is the only thing deciding how many modules the symbol has, and module count against printed size is the only thing deciding whether a phone reads it - in the 10 mm title block the code is the strip's height less two modules of quiet zone above and below. TrueVision's printed address is 42 bytes, EXACTLY what a version 3 symbol holds at error correction M: 29 modules, 0.303 mm each; its full app address was 135 bytes, version 8, 49 modules, 0.19 mm, which no phone reads. FOR VALE: the candidate DR-12 names, a q/ page on ValeCodebase's GitHub Pages with a four or five character key, is 52 or 53 bytes - version 4, 33 modules, 0.270 mm, under the 0.28 mm floor (DR-12 pairs that address with a 0.265 mm floor); keyed by the address bar's token instead (2026/57994__Harris__Scheme-02) it would be 79 bytes, version 5, 0.244 mm; a short domain of Vale's own, about 21 bytes, would be version 2, 25 modules, 0.345 mm. Na__Test__ProjectQr__.test.mjs measures the candidate, the token form and the floor with the encoder itself.
ProjectQr__Link__Config.ProjectQr__Link__IndexUrlNote: EMPTY: no resolver index yet, so the check is off (an empty string is an answer: no index, no check). Once the resolver exists (package W5-05) this is its index, relative to this system's folder, so it is found on the live site and on the local Flask server alike. On the authoring machine this system reads it once per project and says so on the console if the project on screen is missing from it, or is listed under a different folder or year - because a drawing exported then would carry a code that opens nothing. It lists each key under projects as { projectFolder, projectYear }, the year in four digits as ValeVision's project loader answers it ('2026'), and it is written by the index writer, never by hand.

ProjectQr__Symbol__Config.ProjectQr__Symbol__Description: How the symbol is drawn, wherever it is drawn. Always vector: one filled path on the screen sheet, in a PDF and in an HTML page, never a raster.
ProjectQr__Symbol__Config.ProjectQr__Symbol__DarkColourNote: Pure black, not the sheet's ink colour (#172b3a), on purpose. A mono laser prints a colour as a halftone screen, and at a third of a millimetre per module a screen's dots are a real fraction of the module: the edges a camera has to find come out ragged. Black prints solid on every printer. Beside the navy text of the title block the difference cannot be seen; to a phone in a site cabin it is the difference that matters.
ProjectQr__Symbol__Config.ProjectQr__Symbol__PortalDarkColourNote: The dark modules of a code a VECTOR carries (Shape__Qr), which is the parametric scrapbook's Project Portal block in both its forms - and only that. hsl(0, 0%, 35%). Adam, 21-Sep-2026: 'instead of them being absolute black, make them softer ... so that they don't look so stark on the page and they still scan fine', after retouching one to this grey in Photoshop and scanning it. The title block's code keeps DarkColour. WHY THE PORTAL MAY BE SOFTER WHEN THE TITLE BLOCK MAY NOT: DarkColourNote's halftone screen, but at the Portal's size. Its smallest code, 15 mm, prints a 0.52 mm module and 20 mm (as dropped) 0.69 mm, where the title block prints 0.30 - so a laser's screen dots are a far smaller fraction of each module. Against the white it is 90 per cent symbol contrast (ISO/IEC 15415 grade A starts at 70). Na__Test__ProjectQr__.test.mjs holds it to that floor and Na__Test__ProjectQr__Decode__.py reads every case back at this grey as well as at black. Painted at painting time, so a block already on a sheet takes a new value on its next repaint with nothing to rebuild.
ProjectQr__Symbol__Config.ProjectQr__Symbol__QuietZoneModulesNote: The clear light margin a document keeps round the symbol, in modules. The title block sizes its code FROM this - the square is the strip's height less this many modules above and below - so it is a layout value, not advice: 2 modules in the 10 mm strip is a 0.61 mm margin round an 8.79 mm code, which is Lantern Designer's 0.6 mm and 8.8 mm arrived at by rule rather than typed in. ISO/IEC 18004 asks for 4. Two is what Lantern Designer has printed since August 2026 (0.6 mm round a 0.267 mm module), which Adam reports scanning fine, and what this system was proved at (see MinModuleMmNote); 4 was tried first and made the title block's margins look, in Adam's words, in need of being 'considerably tighter'. A document that leaves less than this says so on the console. The HTML painter builds the ISO 4 into the symbol's own viewBox, because a web page has the room.
ProjectQr__Symbol__Config.ProjectQr__Symbol__MinModuleMmNote: The smallest printed module a document should give the symbol, in millimetres. A document that draws the symbol smaller is told so on the console, once, with the size it would need - so a title block made lower, or an address made longer, cannot quietly take the code below what a phone can read. WHERE 0.28 COMES FROM: the shipped title block prints a version 3 symbol at 0.303 mm, and Lantern Designer's 33 module symbol prints at 0.267 mm in the same 8.8 mm square, which Adam reports 'working okay in the end'. The floor sits between the two, so the shipped drawing passes and the first thing to make it worse - a fifth character in a project code, which is version 4 and 0.270 mm in this strip - is reported. HOW IT WAS PROVED is in README__ProjectQrCode__.md: real exported PDFs rasterised by PyMuPDF and read by OpenCV, a far fussier reader than a phone, with not one wrong read. 80__Testing__PrototypeEnvironment/Na__Test__ProjectQr__.test.mjs holds this file to these numbers on every run. IN VALEVISION, where no code is printed yet, the floor is TrueVision's: the Vale candidate address (a q/ page on ValeCodebase's GitHub Pages, version 4, 0.270 mm in this strip) would be reported by this guard, and DR-12 pairs that address with a 0.265 mm floor - a change for package W5-05 if that address is chosen.

ProjectQr__Note__Config.ProjectQr__Note__Description: The words that go with the code, so every document in the pack says the same thing beside it. {document} is what the reader is holding: a drawing sheet passes nothing and gets DefaultDocumentNoun, the Drawing Register and the Project Specification pass their own.
ProjectQr__Note__Config.ProjectQr__Note__HeadingTextNote: Adam, 20-Sep-2026: 'Navigate' for 'View' - it sounds better, and it is what the reader is being offered: a model to walk round, not a picture to look at.
ProjectQr__Note__Config.ProjectQr__Note__BodyText: Scan this {document} to enter the 3D model and view the building in full 3D, and to freely navigate and take a tour.
ProjectQr__Note__Config.ProjectQr__Note__CompactTextNote: All there is room for where a document can spare the code a caption and no more. A drawing on A4 turns it up the code's left side, where the whole note would have cut the fields of the title block short. It has the code's own 8.8 mm to run along, which is eight capitals and not a sentence.
